```{r}
#| label: setup-housing
#| include: false
# The data of the housing-audit case and the figures drawn from them, read
# once for every segment of the case. Comes after the shared setup chunk and
# uses its palette, theme and number formats. The files and their codebooks
# are in cases/housing/data/, written by R/housing/ (menu_options.csv by
# hand); every number on the slides is computed from them or taken from
# _planning/housing/housing-facts.md. Estimates are in percentage points, and a
# negative estimate means that Hispanic names were greeted by name less often,
# the direction of the claim.
# The addresses of the case, which the shared segments print
case_vars <- yaml::read_yaml("../_variables.yml")$cases$housing

# readr rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA
curve <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange("b_pp") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(rank = 1:n())
curve_ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
# The twins of the reference specification that count every delivered email,
# and that fit a logit without covariates and with the hard-to-find address
curve_ref_all <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                              uncoded = "drop", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))
twin_logit_none <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "replies",
                                                                uncoded = "drop", model = "logit", adjust = "none"))
twin_logit_email <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "replies",
                                                                 uncoded = "drop", model = "logit", adjust = "email"))

analysts <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
names_disp <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_names.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
subgroups <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_subgroups.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ri <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_ri.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
power <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_power.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
menu_opts <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
audit <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/housing_audit.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
original <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# The published result and the five reanalyses, each placed by its gap in
# points. Marks within 0.05 points of one another share one tag, because the
# published result, UYV3F and P9W8Y all sit at the raw gap of the paper.
marks_all <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/reference_marks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(
    tag = dplyr::if_else(id == "OA", "OAs 2017", id),
    p = dplyr::case_when(
      statistic_type %in% c("z", "t") ~ 2 * pnorm(-abs(statistic)),
      statistic_type == "chi2" ~ pchisq(statistic, 1, lower.tail = FALSE),
      .default = pchisq(statistic, 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
    ),
    sig = p < 0.05,
    rank = purrr::map_int(b_pp, \(x) sum(curve$b_pp < x - 1e-9)) + 0.5
  )
# the marks of the original data; the replication (SCORE) comes from new data
marks <- datawizard::data_filter(marks_all, on_chart & id != "SCORE")
mark_score <- datawizard::data_filter(marks_all, id == "SCORE")

# One value of a record or display file, for inline use
an <- \(id_code, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id_code]
mark_of <- \(id_code, col) marks_all[[col]][marks_all$id == id_code]
grp <- \(group_code, col) names_disp[[col]][names_disp$level == "group" & names_disp$group == group_code]
out_of <- \(outcome_code, contrast_code, col) {
  outcomes[[col]][outcomes$outcome == outcome_code & outcomes$contrast == contrast_code]
}
sub_of <- \(pattern, col) subgroups[[col]][startsWith(subgroups$subgroup, pattern)][1]
pw <- \(design_code, gap) power$power[startsWith(power$design, design_code) & power$gap_pp == gap]
dev_of <- \(option_code, col) deviations[[col]][deviations$option == option_code & deviations$option != deviations$baseline]
fmt_p <- \(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else paste("p =", fmt_num(p, 3))

# Task 3: the value recorded for 8PTRZ, from the public file of the original
# authors – Hispanic against all other names, among the replies with a
# greeting code. chisq.test() applies the continuity correction to a 2 x 2
# table unless told otherwise.
coded_original <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Response_Dichotomous == 1 & !is.na(ProperName)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = startsWith(TreatmentGroup, "Hispanic"))
tab_8ptrz <- stats::xtabs(~ hispanic_name + ProperName, data = coded_original)  # r-style: keep – the table that chisq.test() takes
chi_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz)$statistic)
chi_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# The reference comparison refitted with conventional errors, beside the HC2
# errors of the curve, for the slide on standard errors
ref_rows <- audit |>
  datawizard::data_filter(group %in% c("white", "hispanic") & reply == 1 & !is.na(named)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic = as.integer(group == "hispanic"))
se_conventional <- parameters::model_parameters(stats::lm(named ~ hispanic, data = ref_rows)) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Parameter == "hispanic") |>
  datawizard::data_extract("SE") * 100
logit_ref <- parameters::model_parameters(stats::glm(named ~ hispanic, family = stats::binomial(), data = ref_rows),
                                          ci_method = "wald") |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Parameter == "hispanic")
tab_ref <- stats::xtabs(~ hispanic + named, data = ref_rows)  # r-style: keep – the table that chisq.test() takes
chi_ref_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_ref, correct = FALSE)$statistic)
chi_ref_p <- stats::chisq.test(tab_ref, correct = FALSE)$p.value

# The randomisation distribution of the reference gap. A reshuffle can
# reproduce the observed gap exactly, so the comparison allows for the last
# bits of floating-point error.
ri_band <- stats::quantile(ri$b_pp, c(0.025, 0.975))
ri_extreme <- sum(abs(ri$b_pp) >= abs(curve_ref$b_pp) - 1e-9)

# The names of the six senders in the order of the paper, the Hispanic names
# last; the curve, the marks and the class chart share one visual grammar
name_order <- c("Brett", "Emily", "Tyrone", "Shanice", "Santiago", "Gabriela")
group_cols <- c(white = ncl_blue, black = "#4a78ab", hispanic = burgundy)
plain <- "#1f5fa8"
pop_cols <- c(replies = "#0e3b6a", all = "#2b8585")
pop_labels <- c(replies = "replies only", all = "all delivered emails")

# The curve of 64: one mark per specification, ranked by the estimate, an
# open circle for p < 0.05 under the test of its own model and a cross
# otherwise. `colour_by` = "population" colours the marks by the emails
# counted. coord_cartesian() fixes the range, so that an overlay never
# rescales the axis between consecutive slides.
curve_base <- function(colour_by = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(curve, ggplot2::aes(rank, b_pp)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.4)
  p <- if (is.null(colour_by)) {
    p + ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = sig), colour = plain, alpha = 0.45, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8)
  } else {
    p + ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = sig, colour = .data[[colour_by]]), alpha = 0.75, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9) +
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pop_cols, labels = pop_labels, breaks = names(pop_cols), name = NULL)
  }
  p +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 4), breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE),
                       labels = c("p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) fmt_num(x, 0)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = sprintf("specification, ranked by the estimate (%d)", nrow(curve)),
         y = "Hispanic minus comparison\nnames (points)") +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-24, 3), xlim = c(0, nrow(curve) + 1)) +
    theme_slide(15) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "right",
          legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, -6, 0))
}

# Reference results as ink marks at the end of a thin line to a tag. Marks at
# the same height share a tag, and tags alternate between two heights from
# left to right, so that neighbours on the curve do not crowd one another.
mark_layer <- function(m) {
  tags <- m |>
    dplyr::mutate(spot = round(b_pp, 1)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(rank = mean(rank), b_pp = mean(b_pp), sig = all(sig),
              label = paste(tag, collapse = " · "), .by = spot) |>
    dplyr::arrange(rank) |>
    dplyr::mutate(lab_y = b_pp + rep(c(5.5, 9), length.out = n()))
  list(
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = tags, ggplot2::aes(x = rank, xend = rank, y = b_pp, yend = lab_y),
                 colour = "#9aa3ab", linewidth = 0.35, inherit.aes = FALSE),
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = m, ggplot2::aes(x = rank, y = b_pp), shape = 1, colour = ink,
               size = 3.4, stroke = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE),
    ggplot2::geom_label(data = tags, ggplot2::aes(x = rank, y = lab_y, label = label), colour = ink,
               fill = "#FFFFFFE6", size = 3.7, linewidth = 0.2, hjust = 0,
               inherit.aes = FALSE)
  )
}

# The causal graph of the experiment. The name, the reply and the greeting sit
# on one line; the official (unobserved) forks above it and the community
# below; the arrow that the claim is about arcs over the top. With `among =
# "replies"`, the reply is boxed: the two paths that the box opens, through
# the official and through the community, are drawn in red, and the path
# through the reply, which the box closes, in pale grey.
case_dag <- function(among = c("all", "replies")) {
  among <- match.arg(among)
  nodes <- tibble::tribble(
    ~name,       ~x,   ~y,    ~role,
    "name",      0,    0,     "exposure",
    "reply",     1.6,  0,     "observed",
    "greeting",  3.2,  0,     "outcome",
    "official",  2.4,  1.15,  "unobserved",
    "community", 2.4,  -1.15, "observed"
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(half_w = 0.12 + 0.052 * nchar(name), half_h = 0.2)
  edges <- tibble::tribble(
    ~from,       ~to,
    "name",      "reply",
    "reply",     "greeting",
    "official",  "reply",
    "official",  "greeting",
    "community", "reply",
    "community", "greeting"
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(state = dplyr::case_when(among == "all" ~ "plain",
                             from == "reply" ~ "blocked",
                             .default = "opened"))
  # how far along a unit vector (ux, uy) the edge of a box lies
  to_edge <- \(ux, uy, w, h) pmin(w / pmax(abs(ux), 1e-9), h / pmax(abs(uy), 1e-9))
  tails <- dplyr::select(nodes, from = name, x0 = x, y0 = y, w0 = half_w, h0 = half_h)
  heads <- dplyr::select(nodes, to = name, x1 = x, y1 = y, w1 = half_w, h1 = half_h)
  segs <- edges |>
    dplyr::left_join(tails, by = "from") |>
    dplyr::left_join(heads, by = "to") |>
    dplyr::mutate(len = sqrt((x1 - x0)^2 + (y1 - y0)^2),
           ux = (x1 - x0) / len, uy = (y1 - y0) / len,
           s0 = to_edge(ux, uy, w0, h0) + 0.02,
           s1 = to_edge(ux, uy, w1, h1) + 0.06,
           x = x0 + s0 * ux, y = y0 + s0 * uy,
           xend = x1 - s1 * ux, yend = y1 - s1 * uy)
  edge_cols <- c(plain = "grey40", blocked = "grey82", opened = d_red)
  node_fill <- c(exposure = ncl_blue, outcome = burgundy, observed = "grey45", unobserved = "grey88")
  node_text <- c(exposure = "white", outcome = "white", observed = "white", unobserved = "grey25")
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("curve", x = 0.25, y = 0.24, xend = 2.78, yend = 0.26, curvature = -0.42,
             colour = green, linewidth = 1, linetype = "22",
             arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(8, "pt"), type = "closed")) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 1.6, y = 1.48, label = "the claim: does the name change the greeting?",
             colour = green, fontface = "bold", size = 4.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = segs, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, colour = state),
                 linewidth = 0.9, arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(8, "pt"), type = "closed")) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = edge_cols, guide = "none")
  if (among == "replies") {
    p <- p + ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = 1.6 - 0.62, xmax = 1.6 + 0.62, ymin = -0.36, ymax = 0.36,
                      fill = NA, colour = d_red, linewidth = 1.3)
  }
  p +
    ggplot2::geom_label(data = nodes, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = name, fill = role),
               colour = node_text[nodes$role], fontface = "bold", size = 6, linewidth = 0,
               label.r = grid::unit(5, "pt"), label.padding = grid::unit(7, "pt")) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = node_fill, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.6, 3.8), ylim = c(-1.5, 1.75)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void()
}
```
